text: Which researcher has earned the title "the Godfather of AI"?
explanation: Hinton spent decades on neural networks while almost nobody else did, including through both of the field's winters, and then supervised the work that produced AlexNet in 2012. He shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics with John Hopfield, and he has been blunt about the safety risks ever since.

text: Which researcher built the ImageNet dataset and has been called the Godmother of AI?
explanation: Li started building ImageNet in 2007 and it is hard to overstate what it did, because most of modern computer vision only became possible once the data existed. She has spent the last several years arguing that the bottleneck has moved from algorithms to data quality, and that the next ImageNet has not been built yet.

text: In 2024, which AI researcher shared the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for work on protein structure prediction?
explanation: In 2024 Hassabis and John Jumper shared half the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, and David Baker took the other half for computational protein design. AlphaFold had already predicted the structure of over 200 million proteins by then, which is close to every protein catalogued by hand.

text: Which researcher co-created AlexNet alongside Alex Krizhevsky and Geoffrey Hinton?
explanation: Sutskever was a graduate student at Toronto at the time, and AlexNet is one of the most cited papers in the whole field. He went on to co-found OpenAI, lead the company that made the GPT models, and spend a decade convinced that scaling alone would get to something extraordinary.

text: Which researcher founded DAIR, the Distributed AI Research Institute, and is known for work on algorithmic bias?
explanation: Gebru co-founded Black in AI and led a research team at Google that was pushed out over a paper about the risks of large language models. DAIR came out of that, and the firing became the most public argument anyone in the field has had about what research is allowed to say out loud.

text: Which scholar won the 1978 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences and is known for bounded rationality?
explanation: Simon argued that people satisfice, they look for good enough rather than optimal, and he said the same thing about machines. He and Allen Newell built the Logic Theorist and GPS, and both of them are on the short list of anyone trying to explain where the idea of a thinking machine came from.

text: Who has been the chief executive officer of OpenAI since 2019?
explanation: Altman became CEO in 2019, a year after OpenAI was founded as a nonprofit research lab with the explicit goal of not pursuing profit. That structure has been rewritten twice since, and the board upheaval in November 2023 was the loudest argument anybody has had about who actually controls the company.

text: Which English mathematician designed the Turing test and is regarded as the father of theoretical computer science?
explanation: Turing formalized the idea of a general purpose computing machine and helped break the Enigma code at Bletchley Park. He proposed the imitation game in 1950, and six years later he wrote a paper on machine learning that is the reason the term exists at all.

text: Which researcher was a cofounder and head of Google Brain, and later served as Chief Scientist at Baidu?
explanation: Ng ran Google Brain when the company was largely still using speech and ads research, then spent three years at Baidu before leaving to work on education. He also co-founded Coursera and Deeplearning.ai, which is why his name shows up in far more machine learning course syllabuses than research papers.

text: Which researcher co-founded Anthropic with his sister, and had previously been vice president of research at OpenAI?
explanation: Dario and Daniela Amodei founded Anthropic in January 2021 with the stated goal of promoting AI safety, and he ran research at OpenAI first. Their publishing agenda, Constitutional AI in particular, has been the most sustained public attempt so far to write alignment research down instead of only doing it.

text: Who founded the community blog LessWrong and co-founded the Machine Intelligence Research Institute?
explanation: Yudkowsky founded LessWrong in 2009 using his own posts as seed material, and co-founded MIRI to work on friendly AI. Robin Hanson is the tempting miss because he co-wrote the predecessor blog Overcoming Bias, but he kept that blog while Yudkowsky launched LessWrong. Yudkowsky also spread rationalist ideas through the fanfiction novel Harry Potter and the Methods of Rationality.

text: Who wrote the 2014 book Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies?
explanation: Bostrom, then at Oxford, published Superintelligence in 2014 and it became a New York Times bestseller that carried AI risk into the mainstream. Yudkowsky is the closest miss because his writing on intelligence explosion influenced the book, but he never wrote it. The paperclip maximizer thought experiment comes from Bostrom's work on the orthogonality thesis.

text: Who developed convolutional neural networks in the 1980s and served as Meta chief AI scientist?
explanation: LeCun invented convolutional networks at Bell Labs in the late 1980s, including the LeNet system for reading handwritten checks. Hinton is the tempting miss because he shared the 2018 Turing Award with LeCun and Bengio, but his fame rests on backpropagation and deep belief nets rather than CNNs. LeCun joined Facebook in 2013 to found FAIR and served as chief AI scientist for a decade.

text: Who founded the Quebec AI institute Mila and shared the 2018 Turing Award with Hinton and LeCun?
explanation: Bengio founded Mila, the Quebec Artificial Intelligence Institute in Montreal, and split the 2018 Turing Award for deep learning breakthroughs. Hassabis is the closest miss because he is another famous lab leader, but he co-founded DeepMind and won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry instead. Bengio also co-directs the CIFAR Learning in Machines and Brains program with LeCun.

text: Who led Tesla Autopilot vision as director of AI and later became known for the Zero to Hero neural network videos?
explanation: Karpathy, an OpenAI founding member, joined Tesla in 2017 and led the Autopilot vision team until 2022. George Hotz is the tempting miss because he also worked briefly with Musk on driving automation, but he founded comma.ai instead of leading Tesla AI. Karpathy returned to OpenAI in 2023 and later founded the AI education company Eureka Labs in 2024.

text: Which OpenAI CTO became interim CEO immediately after Sam Altman was fired in November 2023?
explanation: Murati, OpenAI CTO since 2022, stepped in as interim CEO on November 17 2023 when the board removed Altman. Emmett Shear is the tempting miss because he held the same interim title days later, but he came from Twitch and was second in the sequence. Murati left OpenAI in September 2024 and founded Thinking Machines Lab in February 2025.

text: Who co-founded Mistral AI in 2023 and serves as its CEO after working at DeepMind Paris?
explanation: Mensch left DeepMind Paris in May 2023 and co-founded Mistral AI with Guillaume Lample and Timothee Lacroix, becoming CEO. Lample is the tempting miss because he is also a Mistral co-founder, but he serves as chief scientist rather than CEO. Under Mensch, Mistral released open-weight models like Mistral 7B and Mixtral and became the flagship of European AI.

text: Who founded the Chinese AI company DeepSeek after building the High-Flyer quantitative hedge fund?
explanation: Liang co-founded the quant fund High-Flyer in 2015 and launched DeepSeek in 2023, funding it from the fund and stockpiling Nvidia chips before export controls. Kai-Fu Lee is the tempting miss because he is the other famous Chinese AI founder-investor, but his company is 01.AI rather than DeepSeek. DeepSeek stunned markets in early 2025 when its R1 reasoning model matched Western rivals at far lower reported cost.

text: Who co-founded DeepMind and Inflection AI and became CEO of Microsoft AI in 2024?
explanation: Suleyman co-founded DeepMind in 2010, left Google in 2022 to co-found Inflection AI, then joined Microsoft in March 2024 to lead Copilot and consumer AI. Shane Legg is the tempting miss because he is the third DeepMind co-founder, but he stayed in research rather than taking the Microsoft role. Suleyman also wrote the 2023 book The Coming Wave about AI risk.

text: Which Transformer co-author left Google to found Character.AI and returned to Google in 2024?
explanation: Shazeer, a Google researcher since 2000 who designed key parts of the Transformer, left in 2021 with Daniel De Freitas to found Character.AI. Llion Jones is the tempting miss because he is another Transformer author who left Google for a startup, but he joined Sakana AI in Tokyo rather than founding Character.AI. Google brought Shazeer back in August 2024 with a licensing deal reported at over 2 billion dollars.

text: Which Transformer paper co-author went on to co-found and lead Cohere as CEO?
explanation: Gomez was a 20-year-old intern at Google Brain when he co-authored Attention Is All You Need in 2017, then co-founded Cohere in 2019 as CEO. Illia Polosukhin is the tempting miss because he is another Transformer author turned founder, but he founded NEAR Protocol rather than Cohere. Cohere focuses on enterprise AI models rather than consumer chatbots.

text: Who succeeded Mira Murati as OpenAI interim CEO during the November 2023 leadership crisis?
explanation: Shear, who co-founded Justin.tv and led Twitch as CEO until 2023, accepted the interim job on November 20 after Murati and left when Altman was reinstated days later. Bret Taylor is the tempting miss because he became board chair in the shake-up, but he never held the CEO title. Shear had publicly estimated a 5 to 50 percent chance of AI-caused doom, which drew attention during his brief tenure.
